note: Unbaked. Speakers HUSH-9 and Drill Worm have no voice mapping yet.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sol. Sal says there’s a way under the dome. Tell me you know where.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Tom. Sit. Not that chair. That chair is Sal’s. I keep it warm for him out of spite.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Okay. Sal and I are cousins. You know that. What you don’t know is what we do between airport runs.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Is it crimes?

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Letters. Eleven years of letters, Snail Mail to Los Angeles, in the trunks of cabs. Nobody ever opened a bag. Nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You’ve been running a secret mail route.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: A dispatch network. We call it the Network. We never came up with a better name.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Sol. Sol, come in. It’s Sal. Cab seven says hi. She’s fine. She’s the only thing in town that’s moving.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Sal. I have Tom, his sister, two nieces, a boyfriend and a dog in my lobby. Say hi.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy! It’s quiet in here. Even the clocks are quiet. Your mother’s in the kitchen. Don’t panic. She’s fine. She just won’t stop baking.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. Can you get me in?

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m under the dome with a shovel and a very worried shopkeeper. I can’t get out. But I can dig toward you.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The Sub-Rail. Sal and I bored a tunnel under the Layover, from both coasts, for a hobby. It was supposed to open in 2031. It meets in the middle, right under the dome.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You built a transcontinental subway. As a hobby.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: We got a very good deal on a drill.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it. Be careful of the worm.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The worm.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The drill. We call her the Dual-Coast Drill. The kids at the depot call her the Worm. She doesn’t love it.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: I need dispatchers. Two of them. Radio only. Somebody has to read me the tunnel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’m extremely good at being in charge.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m in charge of snacks.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. Dispatch is the most important job in the building. If Sol says stay, you stay.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Copy.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Copy copy.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Sol. I am leaving my children with a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Thirty years. Never lost a passenger. Found two in the trunk. Both were fine.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Somehow that is not comforting.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll be on the radio the whole way. Grace, you’re the voice. Rose, you’re the snacks.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snacks are critical infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB. Nara. Amy. With me. We go down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have my thermos. I’m always ready for a tunnel.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara has never been this ready for anything. She is already at the Metro stairs, vibrating.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Out the door, the Metro stairs on the boulevard. Past the turnstile, there’s a door that says EMPLOYEES ONLY. That’s you. You’re employees now.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: EMPLOYEES ONLY. A platform under the boulevard. And a tunnel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have ridden every line in this city. I didn’t know this one existed. I’m a little bit offended.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. Radio check. Say “over.”

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: At the END, Tata. You say it at the end of what you say.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I said it at the end. It was the only thing I said.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snack check! Check your pockets! I put a pretzel in your left one!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...There’s a pretzel in my left pocket.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Good. Okay. Before you go in, I have to tell you something, and I have to say it fast, because Penny made me promise.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nickel. You’re shaking.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: A man in a long coat bought gold coins from our shops. For years. Paid double. Never took his hat off.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Julian Vance.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: We didn’t know. We thought he was a collector. We took the money. And we kept the best coins in the back, in case he ever paid triple.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny called on the Network from under the dome. She said, “Tell Tom we’re sorry.” And then she said, “The drawer is under the counter.”

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Hers and mine. The last of the old gold. They were supposed to be a retirement.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Why bring them?

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Sal says gold remembers being warm. If amber is warmth that got stuck, then gold can give it somewhere to go. He says. I don’t know. He’s a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re giving up your retirement.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: I’m giving up a drawer. It’s the best drawer I ever had. Go. I’ll bring them down behind you. Sol’s driving me to the second mile marker and making me run.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You don’t have to do this.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Yes, I do. Somebody gave me a shop. I’d like to be somebody who gave something back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The tracks run east. We follow the rails.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Stay together. Nobody falls behind. I’ll be counting.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re at mile marker one thousand two hundred and fifty. But the tunnel is forty feet long. Is that normal?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sign says halfway. I’m choosing to believe the sign.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, did you see the stone in the doorway? It’s STANDING. I think it’s the bouncer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re breaking up. Say... over... Tata?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata? I can’t hear the... Tata? Tata?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace? Rose? The radio’s gone. It’s not static. It’s just gone.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: THIS IS A QUIET CAR.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara barks. Nothing comes out. She tries again. Nothing. She looks at her own mouth, deeply offended.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Noise is a leak. Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Who are you?

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the second time today somebody has told me quiet is safe. Marlowe said it too.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. We are a very good team. Please lower your voices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re being pretty quiet right now.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: You are breathing audibly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I teach third grade. I know what a person sounds like right before they say “be quiet.” You’re in the wrong tunnel.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: I have given the Drill a chip. It no longer digs toward a place. It digs toward the noise. Please observe the quiet. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He left the quiet on. Is anybody else’s ears ringing?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The chip makes it listen for noise. So we make a lot of it. Loudly. Together.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve been trying to get Rose to use her indoor voice for six years. I’m glad somebody finally wants her outdoor one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A cavern. A wall of amber the size of a house. And a hole in the dirt exactly the width of a drill.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That is the biggest drill I have ever seen.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s a Dual-Coast Drill. They went with the budget model. I can tell by the bolts.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s not charging. It’s digging in place. Round and round.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Its lamps are pointed at the amber. Like it wants to dig through and can’t.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s been drilling at that wall for years. Nobody told it to stop.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sits very still. She has never seen anything so large that wanted so little.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hit it if it hits back. Be kind first. Amy, heal. TNB, I’m on the chip. Everybody make some noise.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up, everybody. Walk it off. It brings the roof down every third turn. Heal before, not after.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: ...Five? Five minutes. Nobody ever told me I could stop.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: I’ve been drilling since 1952. I don’t even remember what I was looking for.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Union rules. Hydrate. And when you’re ready, we’ll tell you where you were going.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: ...Bit’s down. Engine’s off. I wasn’t going anywhere. I was just digging in.

lines.speaker: Drill Worm
lines.text: I’m sorry about the roof.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s fine. Nobody’s mad at a drill. They’re mad at whoever put a chip in it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A little grey cube just popped out of its side. The hush chip. It’s very quiet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Not anymore.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA! We can hear you! Sol says the radio is back! I ate a snack for you!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re loud and clear. What happened? Say over. At the END.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We took care of it. Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: See? You can do it.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Sol drove me to the second mile marker and made me run. I have never been so tired and so right.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Mine are in this bag. Penny’s are on the other side of that wall.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The amber is clear on one side. There’s a pocket behind it. Two people are in it. One of them is waving a shovel.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: (through the glass) TOMMY! Over here! Hi! Don’t hug the amber, it’s sticky!

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: (through the glass) Tom! I’m so sorry! Nickel, hold up the drawer! I’ve got mine!

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Hers and mine. On three.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: (through the glass) One. Two. Don’t think about the interest. Three.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The coins glow, and then they run. Gold down the glass like honey. The amber sighs and opens. Right at the height of a door.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: It worked! Gold remembers being warm! I told you! Nobody ever believes the cab driver!

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: Nickel.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: I was saving for a boat.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: You don’t know how to drive a boat.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: That’s why it was a savings.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy. Sol and I started this tunnel in 2011 with a shovel and a very good deal on a drill. I never thought anyone would walk through it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. You’re the reason I got home.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m a cab driver. That’s the whole job.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: Tom. I’m sorry. I sold him the coins. I took the money and I didn’t ask.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You gave back the best drawer you ever had. We’re square.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: It was a very good drawer.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Can I say something? I’ve spent a lot of time fixing mugs somebody dropped. You don’t get the mug back. You get a better mug, with a gold line where it broke.

lines.speaker: Penny
lines.text: That’s a very nice way to say it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s called kintsugi. It’s also called Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: TNB. You fought like somebody who’s done it his whole life.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’ve carried a lot of coffee in my life. It’s mostly timing.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You fix things. That’s good. Nobody fixes things anymore. They throw them out and buy a new one.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m worried about him. About Tom. He says he’s fine. He’s not very good at saying the other thing.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom is worried about everyone except himself. We take turns. You’re on the schedule now.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’d like that.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I’m standing right here.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice schedule.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Okay. The Sub-Rail runs the rest of the way, up under Grump Hollow. It comes out at the breach. Sol’s putting the girls on the five fifteen handcar.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We heard the whole thing. Mommy. We are coming. Do not do anything dramatic.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Copy copy! Tata, I have a pretzel for Nara!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Grace. Rose. You stay with Sol until the handcar. I love you. I’m not being dramatic.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You’re being a little dramatic.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: A little.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rivituso Row. The tomatoes are fine. The peppers are fine. Everything is exactly where it was.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And nothing is moving.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The sprinkler. Every drop is hanging in the air. It’s the prettiest thing I’ve ever seen and I hate it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s so quiet. This is the quietest place I’ve ever been. And I live near a freeway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Halt.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Dad? What are you wearing?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Warden’s plate. Gold. It hums. I like the hum.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My back doesn’t hurt, Tommy. It’s been eleven years. I made a deal.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: What deal?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody gets hurt. Nobody gets old. Nobody gets left. Your mother’s inside. She’s fine. She’s making a crisp.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I stand here and the glass stays up. That’s the deal.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. That isn’t safe. That’s a freezer.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Go home, Tom. Take your friends. Go back to the good coast.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Dad. Take that off. You’ll rust.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Amy. You’re not supposed to be here. You’re supposed to be safe.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’m supposed to be your daughter.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Go home.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He said go home. Twice. That’s a man who wants an argument.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He’s my dad. He wants a lot of arguments.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’re not leaving. We always make our connection.
